blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#477 merge SHA (dispatch-only
    # CI + sticky approval latches — the SM is the only CI trigger, no
    # re-review after the first approval; supersedes #466).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@7fe0a64eed91a0a56260802f836b9295ddb15c98
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 7fe0a64eed91a0a56260802f836b9295ddb15c98
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# Machine merge bot stub — event-driven fast path (factory pack).
#
# The SM cron tick is best-effort (GitHub silently drops scheduled runs);
# this workflow reacts to EVENTS: CI conclusion, label changes, head

# Idempotent against the SM: shared labels, first actor wins.
name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:
    types: [labeled, synchronize, edited]
  check_run:
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch: {}

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@68d98b0461944c6f48a7699e0eb35d5344bfeed6
    with:
      factory_ref: 68d98b0461944c6f48a7699e0eb35d5344bfeed6
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no Machine SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch
#      one tick and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the three required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch ci.yml on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: SM kicker

run-name: 🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: machine-sm.yml / ci.yml
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/machine-sm.yml/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run machine-sm.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == "CI" and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name | select(. == "Quality gate" or . == "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" or . == "Binaries smoke gate")] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == "CI")] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run ci.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

blocks.text:
# Merge Trigger — GitHub-issues tracker variant (machine-kit).
#
# Placeholder tokens (rendered by machine-kit/setup.sh):
#   CI — the workflow whose green run arms the trigger
#                            (e.g. "Quality" in dmtools-dart, "CI" elsewhere)
#
# The tracker is THIS repo's GitHub issues (no Jira, no external services):
#
#   issue labeled `pr_approved` → linked PR found → required checks green
#   (branch protection is the gate: mergeStateStatus CLEAN) → squash-merge →
#   label removed → comment posted on the issue.
#
# Linking conventions (either works):
#   - PR body contains `Closes #NN` / `Fixes #NN` / `Resolves #NN`
#   - PR branch name starts with `NN-` (e.g. `42-fix-foo`)
#
# Prerequisites:
#   vars: MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED (fuse — job skips itself until `true`)
#   branch protection on main with required checks + strict (the machine
#   only merges CLEAN PRs, so protection defines what "ready" means).
#   No secrets needed: github.token is sufficient (merge + issues + PR write).
#   Branch freshness is the SM's job (silent-update-behind); CI on the refreshed
#   head is re-dispatched by the SM (dispatch-only CI — pushes fire no
#   workflows; auto-update-prs.yml is retired).

name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same-repo guard: PRs from forks must not trigger merges.
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    concurrency:
      group: merge-trigger-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Gate on MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED
        id: gate
        env:
          ENABLED: ${{ vars.MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::merge-trigger scaffold is wired but disabled — set the MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED repo variable to true (after branch protection + required checks are in place)."
          fi

      - name: Merge issues labeled pr_approved
        if: steps.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token }}
          LABEL: pr_approved
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          issues=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
            --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ -z "$issues" ]; then
            echo "no issues labeled '$LABEL' — nothing to merge"
            exit 0
          fi
          merged=0; skipped=0
          for n in $issues; do
            echo "::group::issue #$n"
            pr=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
              [.[]
                | select(
                    ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$n"'\\b"))
                    or (.headRefName | test("^'"$n"'[-_.]"))
                  )
                | .number] | first // empty')
            if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
              echo "issue #$n: no linked open PR (add 'Closes #$n' to the PR body or name the branch '$n-…') — skipping"
              skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "::endgroup::"; continue
            fi
            state=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" \
              --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus \
              --jq '.mergeable + ":" + .mergeStateStatus')
            echo "linked PR #$pr — $state"
            case "$state" in
              MERGEABLE:CLEAN)
                if err=$(gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" --squash 2>&1); then
                  merged=$((merged+1))
                  gh issue edit "$n" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$repo" \
                    --body "🔀 Merged #$pr (CI: ${CI_RUN_URL:-run})" || true
                  echo "✅ merged #$pr for issue #$n"
                else
                  skipped=$((skipped+1))
                  echo "❌ merge of #$pr failed: $err"
                fi
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BEHIND)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ behind main — the SM (silent-update-behind) refreshes it, then re-dispatches CI"
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BLOCKED|MERGEABLE:UNSTABLE)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ required checks not green yet"
                ;;
              *)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⛔ not mergeable ($state) — needs manual attention"
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          echo "summary: merged=$merged skipped=$skipped"

blocks.text:
# Runner split (2026-09-22): PURE-DART jobs -> ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo:
# free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64 queue). Flutter jobs stay x64 —
# Flutter ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable 3.47.5 manifest is x64
# only; subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64').
# cube-kernel-live -> self-hosted M5 (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:

#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov

#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)

# Agents — Developer Documentation This directory contains the configuration and JavaScript logic for the **AI-powered Scrum Master (SM) agent system**. The SM agent orchestrates a fully automated software delivery pipeline: it continuously monitors Jira, triggers specialized AI agents for each workflow stage, and manages the complete lifecycle of Stories, Bugs, and Test Cases from Backlog to Done. --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview](#overview) 2. [Architecture](#architecture) 3. [Pipeline Diagrams](#pipeline-diagrams) - [Story Pipeline](#story-pipeline) - [Bug Pipeline](#bug-pipeline) - [Test Case Pipeline](#test-case-pipeline) 4. [Full System Overview](#full-system-overview) 5. [SM Rules](#sm-rules) 6. [Agent Configs](#agent-configs) 7. [Key JS Scripts](#key-js-scripts) 8. [Label Lifecycle](#label-lifecycle) 9. [Execution Flow](#execution-flow) --- ## Overview The SM agent system automates the Agile delivery workflow by: - Running on a **20-minute schedule** via GitHub Actions (`sm.yml`) - Scanning Jira using per-rule JQL queries defined in `sm.json` - Dispatching the appropriate agent config (via `ai-teammate.yml` workflow dispatch) or running logic locally for fast/safe operations - Using **label-based locking** to prevent duplicate processing of the same ticket - Supporting three agent types: **Teammate** (CLI agent + prompt), **TestCasesGenerator** (DMTools job), and **JSRunner** (pure JS, no AI) The system covers the full lifecycle: backlog refinement, acceptance criteria generation, solution design, development, PR review, test case generation, test automation, and bug management. --- ## Architecture ### SM Agent Loop The SM agent (`smAgent.js`) is the central orchestrator. Every 20 minutes: 1. Reads all rules from `sm.json` 2. For each enabled rule, runs the JQL query against Jira 3. For each matching ticket, checks `skipIfLabel` — skips the ticket if the label is already present (lock is held) 4. Adds `addLabel` to the ticket (acquires lock) 5. Either dispatches a GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` to `ai-teammate.yml` (with `config_file` and `concurrency_key` inputs), executes the JS logic locally (`localExecution: true`), **or** runs the full teammate pipeline synchronously on the local machine (`localTeammate: true`) ### Execution Modes | Mode | When Used | Behavior | |------|-----------|----------| | **Dispatch** (default) | Complex AI tasks (development, review, test gen) | Triggers `ai-teammate.yml` workflow on GitHub Actions; runs asynchronously | | **localExecution: true** | Fast/safe operations (merge checks, status checks) | Runs the postJS directly inside the SM process; synchronous; no AI CLI, no checkout | | **localTeammate: true** | Running the SM/AI Teammate pipeline on a local machine instead of GitHub Actions (e.g. no self-hosted runner available, or for fast local iteration) | Runs `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh`, which calls the same `dmtools run ` entrypoint `ai-teammate.yml` uses — full checkout/branch-switch, AI CLI, PR/Jira actions — but in the calling process. Because it blocks until the script exits, tickets are always processed **one at a time**, regardless of `maxTriggeredWorkflows` (see [Local Execution Flow](#local-teammate-execution-flow-localteammate-true)) | ### Agent Types | Type | Description | |------|-------------| | **Teammate** | Runs a CLI agent (Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Codemie) with a markdown prompt file. `skipAI: true` means AI is driven by the CLI tool, not DMTools AI directly. | | **TestCasesGenerator** | A specialized DMTools job that reads a Jira story/bug and generates structured Test Case tickets (issue type: Test Case) in Jira. | | **JSRunner** | Executes a pure JavaScript file (`jsPath`) with no AI involvement. Used for orchestration (`smAgent.js`) and reporting (`workflowFailureReporter.js`). | ### Concurrency and Locking - **`skipIfLabel`** — SM checks for this label before processing. If present, the ticket is skipped (another run already claimed it). - **`addLabel`** — SM adds this label immediately before dispatching, serving as a distributed lock. - The agent's **postJS** calls `releaseLock()` to remove the label once processing is complete. - The `wip` label (or `_wip`) can be manually applied to any ticket to **pause** SM processing for that ticket indefinitely. --- ## Pipeline Diagrams ### Story Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef humanInput fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#92400e,font-weight:bold classDef action fill:#f0f9ff,stroke:#0ea5e9,color:#0c4a6e classDef status fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d s_bl([Backlog]):::status act_q["story_questions.json · dispatch

CLI-based AI execution: ``` SM Agent (smAgent.js) │ ├─ 1. Run JQL → find matching Jira tickets ├─ 2. For each ticket: │ ├─ Check skipIfLabel → skip if present (ticket is locked) │ ├─ Add addLabel to Jira ticket (acquire lock) │ └─ Dispatch workflow_dispatch to ai-teammate.yml │ inputs: { config_file, concurrency_key } │ ai-teammate.yml (GitHub Actions) │ ├─ 3. Load config_file (e.g., story_development.json) ├─ 4. Run preJSAction (e.g., checkWipLabel.js) │ └─ If wip label found → abort early, release lock ├─ 5. Run preCliJSAction (optional, e.g., fetchQuestionsToInput.js) │ └─ Fetches extra context and injects into prompt variables ├─ 6. Invoke CLI Agent (Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Codemie / Fa) │ └─ Uses cliPrompt markdown file as the task specification │ └─ CLI agent reads Jira ticket, writes code, runs commands ├─ 7. Run postJSAction (e.g., developTicketAndCreatePR.js) │ ├─ Parses CLI agent output │ ├─ Creates PR, posts comments, transitions Jira status, etc. │ └─ Calls releaseLock() → removes addLabel from Jira ticket ``` ### Local Execution Flow (localExecution: true) Used for synchronous, lightweight operations that don't need a full GitHub Actions runner: ``` SM Agent (smAgent.js) │ ├─ 1. Run JQL → find matching Jira tickets ├─ 2. For each ticket: │ ├─ Check skipIfLabel → skip if present │ └─ Run postJS function directly in-process (e.g., retryMergePR.js) │ ├─ No label locking (localExecution rules often omit addLabel) │ ├─ Executes synchronously │ └─ Transitions Jira ticket status or performs merge operation ``` ### Local Teammate Execution Flow (localTeammate: true) Runs the **full** Teammate pipeline (checkout, AI CLI, PR/Jira actions) on the machine that runs the SM job, instead of dispatching `ai-teammate.yml` to GitHub Actions. Useful when there is no GitHub Actions runner available for this workload, or for fast local iteration without waiting on a runner queue. ``` SM Agent (smAgent.js) │ ├─ 1. Run JQL → find matching Jira tickets ├─ 2. For each ticket (processed strictly one at a time — see below): │ ├─ Check skipIfLabel → skip if present (no active-workflow-run recovery check; │ │ that logic only makes sense for async GitHub Actions dispatches) │ ├─ Write the rule's encoded_config to a temp file (agents/.dmtools/local-run-*.json) │ └─ scripts/run-teammate-local.sh --config-file --ticket ... │ ├─ Refuses to run if the working tree is dirty (protects uncommitted work) │ ├─ Syncs the base branch (git fetch + checkout + pull --ff-only) │ ├─ dmtools --debug run [] --inputJql "key = " │ │ (identical entrypoint to ai-teammate.yml's "Run AI Teammate" step — │ │ preJS → CLI agent → postJS all run exactly as they do on a runner) │ └─ Fails loudly if the tree is still dirty afterwards (agent should always │ commit + push everything it changed, same contract as on a runner) └─ 3. addLabel only after a successful local run ``` **Why sequential, not worktree-based:** `cli_execute_command()` blocks until the script exits, and rules with `localTeammate: true` bypass the `maxTriggeredWorkflows` budget entirely (that budget only bounds *outstanding* async GitHub Actions runs). The working copy is reused across tickets — no git worktrees — because the teammate agent's own `postJSAction` always commits and pushes before finishing; the next ticket simply starts from a freshly-synced base branch. **Secrets:** read from the calling shell's environment first; `run-teammate-local.sh` fills in anything missing from `./dmtools.env` (same `KEY=VALUE` format `scripts/run-agent.sh` already loads). Real environment variables always take priority — `dmtools.env` never overrides an already-exported value. Typical required vars: `JIRA_EMAIL`, `JIRA_API_TOKEN`, `JIRA_BASE_PATH`, `GH_TOKEN`/`PAT_TOKEN`, plus whatever the configured `AI_AGENT_PROVIDER` needs (e.g. `COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN`). **Switching an entire SM run to local without editing any rule:** rather than adding `localTeammate: true` to every rule in `sm.json`/`.dmtools/config.js`, pass a CLI JSON override when invoking the SM job. `dmtools run ` deep-merges `` into the *whole* job config object (`{name, params}`), not just into `params.jobParams` directly — so the override must be wrapped in `params` too, mirroring the same shape as the job config file itself: ```bash dmtools run agents/sm.json '{"params":{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}}' ``` A bare `{"jobParams":{"forceLocalTeammate":true}}` (without the outer `params` wrapper) is silently ignored — it doesn't raise an error, the SM job just runs with the unmodified default `jobParams` from `sm.json`, so every rule falls through to its normal dispatch behavior as if the override had never been passed. With `forceLocalTeammate: true`, every default-dispatch rule for that run behaves as if it had `localTeammate: true` — no GitHub Actions dispatch, everything runs through `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` sequentially. Rules already using `localExecution: true` are untouched (they never dispatched in the first place), and any rule can still opt out of the override with an explicit `localTeammate: false`. Without the override, the SM job runs exactly as before — default dispatch to `ai-teammate.yml` — so this is purely an opt-in, per-invocation switch; nothing in `sm.json` or `.dmtools/config.js` needs to change. **Required whitelist entry:** `runTeammateLocally()` (and `localTeammate`/ `forceLocalTeammate` in general) invokes `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh` via `bash agents/scripts/run-teammate-local.sh ...` through the `cli_execute_command` MCP tool. That tool only allows a fixed base whitelist of commands (`git, gh, dmtools, npm, yarn, docker, kubectl, terraform, ansible, aws, gcloud, az`) — `bash` is **not** in it by default, so the very first local run fails with `Command not allowed. Whitelisted commands: ...`. `sm.json`'s top-level `params` therefore sets `"envVariables": {"CLI_ALLOWED_COMMANDS": "bash"}`, which is applied as a thread-local override for the whole SM job run (see `CliCommandExecutor`/`PropertyReader` in `dmtools-core`) and needs no VM-side `dmtools.env` changes — it travels with the repo. ### Bootstrapping a Local/Cloud Dev Session `scripts/warmup-session.sh` prepares a fresh machine (cloud dev-environment session, throwaway VM, container, ...) so that `localTeammate`/`localExecution` rules — or manual `dmtools run` calls — work out of the box. Meant to run once as the "warmup" step of a session template; safe to re-run (idempotent — syncs instead of re-cloning if the target directory already exists). ```bash warmup-session.sh --repo --dir [--branch ] \ [--exclude "tool1 tool2 ..."] [--install-args "extra args for install.sh"] ``` - `--repo` / `--dir` — the product repo to clone (with its `agents` submodule) and the local directory to clone it into. - `--branch` — checkout/track this branch instead of the repo's default. - `--exclude` — space-separated tool names to skip (forwarded to `setup/install.sh all` as `-tool1 -tool2 ...`; see `setup/install.sh` for the full tool list: `java maven node dmtools maestro copilot codemie cursor codegraph playwright kimi gradle android konan`). - `--install-args` — extra raw arguments appended to the `install.sh` invocation. It does **not** create or touch a `dmtools.env` file and does **not** run the agent pipeline — secrets are expected to already be exposed as real environment variables by the session template (`run-agent.sh`/`run-teammate-local.sh` read those directly). See [`scripts/warmup-session.md`](scripts/warmup-session.md) for full worked examples — Bitrise-style Dev Environment templates (warmup/startup script fields + template variables), GitHub Codespaces `devcontainer.json` (`onCreateCommand`/`postStartCommand`), and plain CI/local-machine usage. Pair it with a lightweight "startup" step (run on every session start/restart) that just syncs the repo: ```bash cd && git fetch origin && git checkout && \ git pull --ff-only origin && git submodule update --init --recursive ``` ### TestCasesGenerator Flow ``` [Showing lines 1-869 of 1175 (50.0KB limit). blocks.text:
# gh-939: Add 'blocked' label: SM ignores labeled PRs/issues — manual queue prioritization + CI load control

## Description

Owner proposal (2026-09-25). Today the SM/factory pipeline churns on everything assigned; when an item is not ready (waiting on a dependency, mid-design, parked), CI still burns runner time on it and the queue order is not manually controllable.

## Semantics
- A `blocked` label on an issue or PR means: SM (sm.yml / Machine Merge Bot / any scheduler) IGNORES the item completely:
  - no CI dispatch or re-dispatch for its PR head (also no required-context chasing/reminders);
  - no merge attempt even if checks are green;
  - no pick-up from the issue queue, no progress nagging;
  - for issues with linked PRs — the linked PR inherits the ignore.
- Removing the label returns the item to the queue at its normal position (nothing else changes).
- The label is a HUMAN/owner control: agents/factory must not add or remove it on their own (except the owner or an explicitly instructed session).

## Value
- Manual prioritization: the owner orders the factory's work explicitly (e.g. land #936/#937 first, park #922/#923 for later).
- CI/CD economy: parked PRs stop consuming mini-runner/hosted minutes on re-runs of doomed legs.

## Implementation sketch
- In the merge-bot/scheduler workflow: a pre-step lists labels of the PR/issue (gh api, one call) and skips it if `blocked` present; log 'skipped (blocked)' for observability.
- Cancel-in-progress protection: if a run for a now-blocked PR is already live, let it finish (do not cancel mid-flight).
- Document the label in the factory README/AGENTS so every agent honors it.

Pairs with #938 (test-skip unblock) as part of the CI load-control kit.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/unattended), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
  context hygiene for detours. `CheckpointRewindController` wraps
  `Agent.prepareNextTurn`, persists via host `CheckpointSessionSink`.
  Lifecycle (issue #286): a checkpoint is scoped to its detour — when the
  next `checkpoint` call finds it stale (a user turn arrived inside the
  detour, or the anchored span was rebuilt away by reload/compaction), it
  is auto-closed with a note + `checkpoint_auto_closed` session record
  instead of refusing; `rewind` semantics are unchanged.
- `lib/src/compaction/branch_summarization.dart` — `generateBranchSummary` +
  `navigateSessionTree` (use instead of `Session.moveTo` for tree
  navigation); summary is a `branch_summary` record on the entered branch.
- `lib/src/agent/tool_pairing.dart` — context pair-integrity (issue #85):
  `validateToolPairing` checks the wire-equivalent message sequence (orphan
  results, unanswered calls, duplicate ids, displaced results after
  same-role merges); `repairToolPairing` fixes the outbound payload only
  (drop orphan + note, synthesize interrupted results, hoist steering text
  after results, uniquify duplicate ids symmetrically on call+result).
  `agent_loop.dart` repairs before every request and retries once on a
  pairing-shaped provider 400 (`ToolPairingRepairEvent` is the audit
  trail); `_finishStreamed` stamps per-run position-counter ids
  session-unique; `auto_compactor.dart`'s `_localTrimFallback` routes the
  kept region through the same repairer.
- `lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart` — session image registry (issue
  #171): unique images ride a provider request exactly once; every other
  occurrence becomes a `[Image N]` text ref. `rewriteHistoryImages`
  rewrites the OUTBOUND payload only (session JSONL byte-identical);
  carriers `[{text:"[Image N]"},{image}]` anchor before the first
  referencing user message or after the tool-result run (never inside
  call/result pairs); the current user message rides images in place
  (I3), each in-place image carrying its `[Image N]` label (issue #195
  F3 — the model can cite what it sees); the per-request cap
  (`images.maxPerRequest`, default 20) drops current-first-then-newest
  with a drop notice (never silent; the app logs drops via `AppLog`,
  issue #195 F4); dangling refs (compaction, cap) resolve to `(image no
  longer available)`, and once a renumbering boundary exists (compaction
  summary, structured marker, local-trim note) AUTHORED history
  citations degrade to that note too — after renumbering an `[Image N]`
  may name a different image, so silent rebinding is never allowed
  (issue #195 F2; generated refs/labels stay content-keyed and fresh).
  Stateless per-request rebuild — determinism, compaction eviction and
  resume come free. Kill switch `images.registry: false` → byte-for-byte
  legacy shape. `agent_loop.dart` applies it in `_buildRequestContext`
  after `transformContext`, before tool-pairing repair.
- `lib/src/trajectory/` — the trajectory ledger core (issue #10): finalized
  session records project into an immutable `TrajectorySnapshot` through
  `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder.append`/`applyEvent` — streamed agent events
  land as synthetic rows keyed `turn\0step` (`u\0turn` for prompts) and are
  replaced when the real record lands; revision grows per append. Record
  kinds (closed set, `TrajectoryCellKind`): system, user, context,
  compacted, message, tool, subtool — a subtool is a
  `TrajectoryToolRecord.parentCallId != null`, which only hosts build
  directly (the builder never nests). Derived state folds once per
  snapshot: `deriveTrajectoryLayout` (turns of Message/Step groups +
  collapsible turn/assistant-run summaries), `deriveTrajectoryTimeline`
  (four modes — `sequence` equal-width slots, `duration` with idle gaps
  compressed out, `time` zero-width wall-clock markers, `actual` real gaps;
  three fixed lanes: 0 system/user/context, 1 message/compacted, 2 tools),
  `trajectoryTimelineFocusIndexes` (selection → visible ledger indexes),
  and `ThrottledTrajectorySearchIndex` (full-text; matches are stable
  record ids). `formatters.dart` holds the shared duration/token/throughput
  formatting; `trajectory_preview.dart` the bounded single-line previews;
  `trajectory_export.dart` the whole-snapshot JSON/Markdown exporters the
  header's copy menu uses. Tool records carry `startedAt` (real launch
  time, distinct from the projected position) so the Gantt/actual
  projections plot true spans. Outbound model requests persist for the
  ledger as hidden `model_request_summary` `CustomRecord`s — the CLI
  event handler (`agent_event_handler.dart`, emitted through
  `agent_cli.dart`) and the app's `AgentService` both buffer a
  `TrajectoryRequestDetail` per call and flush it onto the session
  record chain right before the assistant message, so replays see it
  ahead of the reply — and `TrajectorySnapshotBuilder` folds them into
  the message record's request detail (the Request tab).
  Consumers render, never re-derive: `packages/fa_ui`'s
  `lib/src/trajectory/` widgets and the CLI `/trajectory` family.
- `lib/src/cli/trajectory_commands.dart` (a `part of` `agent_cli.dart`) +
  `lib/src/cli/trajectory_tui.dart` — the read-only REPL family
  `/trajectory [view|cost|tail|inspect <n>]` (bare = `view`, capped at 200
  rows; `tail` follows the live session every 500ms) and the headless
  `fa trajectory <view|tail|cost|inspect> [sessionId] [--json] [--at N]`
  subcommand (`--at N` replays the snapshot as it stood at record N, view
  only). Session resolution: exact id > session-name match > most recent.
  Rendering is pure Dart in `trajectory_tui.dart` (no `dart:io`), shared by
  both entries; `bin/fah.dart` routes the subcommand.

blocks.text:
# Machine SM — thin stub over the dmtools-agents factory (reusable pack).
#
# The whole reconcile tick (engine checkout, dmtools install, rule run)
# lives in IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml. This
# file carries only the triggers (cron + manual dry dispatch) and the
# call. NO caller-side concurrency: the factory owns the `machine-sm`
# group — a caller declaring the same group deadlocks the called workflow
# (it waits forever on a group its own caller holds).

name: 'Machine SM'

run-name: >-
  🧹 SM ${{
    github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && 'manual tick' ||
    format('tick {0}', github.event.schedule || '') }}${{
  github.event.inputs.dryRun == 'true' && ' (dry)' || '' }}

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: '*/10 * * * *'   # short ticks — the engine idles when busy
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      dryRun:
        description: 'Log the plan, perform no action'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: true


# The factory's own permissions block cannot raise rights above the
# caller, and the org default caps the token at read-only — the silent
# update-branch path (workflow token, updatePullRequestBranch) failed
# live with "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update
# this pull request" until this explicit block lifted the ceiling.
permissions:
  # contents: write — update-branch pushes a merge commit onto the PR head
  # branch; PullRequests: write alone is denied at the refs level (live:
  # "github-actions[bot] does not have permission to update this pull
  # request" even with PullRequests: write granted).
  contents: write         # checkout + silent update-branch pushes
  issues: write           # labels + close-issue safety net
  pull-requests: write    # update-branch + merge
  checks: write           # bridge-free validation stamps (factory #510):
                          # the reusable factory requests it — the caller
                          # must grant an equal-or-superset or the workflow
                          # dies with startup_failure (live 16:03-16:13 ×3).
  actions: write          # workflow_dispatch on the teammate workflow

jobs:
  sm:
    # Pinned to the immutable dmtools-agents#477 merge SHA (dispatch-only
    # CI + sticky approval latches — the SM is the only CI trigger, no
    # re-review after the first approval; supersedes #466).
    # Flip in lockstep with ai-teammate.yml — guarded by
    # test/machine_kit/factory_stub_ref_test.dart.
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-sm.yml@7fe0a64eed91a0a56260802f836b9295ddb15c98
    with:
      # The literal uses-ref: the factory requires it (it cannot derive its
      # own ref — github.workflow_ref in a called workflow is the CALLER's).
      factory_ref: 7fe0a64eed91a0a56260802f836b9295ddb15c98
      # Manual ticks default to dry; cron ticks run live.
      dryRun: ${{ github.event.inputs.dryRun || 'false' }}
      # #687: one source of truth for the machine login (repo variable).
      machine-author: ${{ vars.MACHINE_AUTHOR || '' }}
      # #687: the workflow token — silent branch updates (pushes trigger
      # no workflows). Input channel: secrets-block mapping arrives empty.
      silent-token: ${{ github.token }}
      # Dispatch-only CI: this repo's CI file (the SM dispatches it on PR
      # heads; default 'quality.yml' fits dmtools-dart, not this repo).
      ci-workflow: ci.yml
      # Bridge-free mode (factory #510): the tick stamps the three required
      # protection checks itself — ci-gate.yml bridge is deleted in this PR.
      validation-checks: '["Quality gate","JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)","Binaries smoke gate"]'
      # Factory-state snapshot → public prerelease asset (board: site/factory)
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
    # Explicit mapping — the factory DECLARES SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN as a
    # required named secret (plus optional ZAI_CODE_KEY / KIMI_REVIEW_KEY),
    # and `secrets: inherit` does not satisfy required-secret validation at
    # call time (live bisect: inherit => startup failure, explicit => green).
    secrets:
      # EXACTLY the set factory-sm.yml declares (SOURCE only) — mapping a
      # secret the callee does not declare is rejected at call time
      # (probe H2: +ZAI/KIMI => startup failure; probe I: exact set => green).
      # NOTE: github.token CANNOT ride this block — GitHub delivers an
      # empty value when it is mapped through a reusable call's secrets
      # (live-verified); it rides the silent-token INPUT below instead.
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: 'Machine Merge Bot'

on:

    workflows: ['CI', 'Quality']   # per-repo: fa's dispatched CI is named 'CI'
    types: [completed]
  pull_request:

  check_run:
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: read
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write

concurrency:
  group: machine-merge-bot
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  merge:
    # Label events only matter for the machine latches; other PR events
    # (synchronize/edited) always run — cheap and idempotent.
    if: >-
      github.event_name != 'pull_request' ||
      github.event.action != 'labeled' ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'ai_') ||
      contains(github.event.label.name, 'pr_approved')
    uses: IstiN/dmtools-agents/.github/workflows/factory-merge.yml@68d98b0461944c6f48a7699e0eb35d5344bfeed6
    with:
      factory_ref: 68d98b0461944c6f48a7699e0eb35d5344bfeed6
      ci_workflow: ci.yml
    secrets:
      SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SOURCE_GITHUB_TOKEN }}

# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires

blocks.text:
# SM kicker — a tiny watchdog (two jobs, seconds each, ~zero runner cost).
#
# Why it exists: this repo's CI is dispatch-only (ci.yml `on.push` fires
# nothing on PR heads) and the Machine SM is the sole trigger. Two gaps
# leave a PR BLOCKED forever with zero required-check contexts on its head:
#
#   1. SM dead: the cron tick missed/failed and nothing re-arms it.
#      Fix: if no Machine SM run is queued/running/in-progress — dispatch
#      one tick and die.
#
#   2. Head completeness: pushes WITHOUT code changes (pure main-merge
#      commits — the SM's own silent update-branch, or a manual
#      "merge main into branch") fire no workflows by design, yet the
#      strict `up-to-date` protection demands FRESH required checks on
#      the new head SHA. The SM's validate-fresh/armed rules don't count
#      a no-code rebase as "validation due", so the contexts never appear.
#      Fix: if a PR head is a codeless merge commit (2 parents, 0 files
#      vs first parent) and carries NEITHER of the three required check
#      contexts NOR an active CI run — dispatch ci.yml on that head.
#
# Code-bearing pushes (dev/rework/WIP) are deliberately NOT touched here:
# their validation schedule stays owned by the SM ("intermediate pushes
# are free"). The schedule leg re-checks open PRs every 30 min to also
# cover bot pushes made with GITHUB_TOKEN (those fire no events at all).

name: SM kicker

run-name: 🥁 kicker ${{ github.event_name }} ${{ github.ref_name }}

on:
  push:
    branches-ignore: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: '13,43 * * * *'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write        # workflow_dispatch: machine-sm.yml / ci.yml
  contents: read
  pull-requests: read
  checks: read

concurrency:
  group: sm-kicker
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}

jobs:
  sm-liveness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch an SM tick if none is queued or running
        run: |
          active=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/workflows/machine-sm.yml/runs?per_page=1" \
            --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending")] | length')
          if [ "${active:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "SM alive ($active active run(s)) — nothing to do"
          else
            echo "SM idle — dispatching a tick"
            gh workflow run machine-sm.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"
          fi

  head-completeness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Dispatch CI on codeless PR heads that carry no required contexts
        run: |
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "push" ]; then
            if [ "$GITHUB_REF_TYPE" != "branch" ]; then echo "tag push — skip"; exit 0; fi
            branches=("${GITHUB_REF_NAME}")
          else
            mapfile -t branches < <(gh pr list -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --state open --json headRefName --jq '.[].headRefName')
            echo "scanning ${#branches[@]} open PR branch(es)"
          fi
          for b in "${branches[@]}"; do
            sha=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$b" --jq .sha 2>/dev/null) || { echo "$b: no head, skip"; continue; }
            read -r parents files < <(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha" --jq '"\(.parents | length) \(.files | length)"')
            if [ "$parents" != "2" ] || [ "${files:-1}" != "0" ]; then
              echo "$b: code-bearing head — SM owns validation, skip"
              continue
            fi
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == "CI" and (.status == "in_progress" or .status == "queued" or .status == "waiting" or .status == "pending"))] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI already active on ${sha:0:9} — skip"
              continue
            fi
            found=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/commits/$sha/check-runs?per_page=100" \
              --jq '[.check_runs[].name | select(. == "Quality gate" or . == "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)" or . == "Binaries smoke gate")] | length')
            if [ "${found:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: ${sha:0:9} already has required contexts — skip"
              continue
            fi
            # grace re-check: a CI dispatch may be in flight from the SM/chain
            sleep 45
            ci=$(gh api "repos/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY/actions/runs?head_sha=$sha&event=workflow_dispatch" \
              --jq '[.workflow_runs[] | select(.name == "CI")] | length')
            if [ "${ci:-0}" -gt 0 ]; then
              echo "$b: CI appeared during grace window — skip"
              continue
            fi
            echo "$b: codeless head ${sha:0:9} with zero required contexts — dispatching CI"
            gh workflow run ci.yml -R "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --ref "$b"
          done

blocks.text:
# Merge Trigger — GitHub-issues tracker variant (machine-kit).
#
# Placeholder tokens (rendered by machine-kit/setup.sh):
#   CI — the workflow whose green run arms the trigger
#                            (e.g. "Quality" in dmtools-dart, "CI" elsewhere)
#
# The tracker is THIS repo's GitHub issues (no Jira, no external services):
#
#   issue labeled `pr_approved` → linked PR found → required checks green
#   (branch protection is the gate: mergeStateStatus CLEAN) → squash-merge →
#   label removed → comment posted on the issue.
#
# Linking conventions (either works):
#   - PR body contains `Closes #NN` / `Fixes #NN` / `Resolves #NN`
#   - PR branch name starts with `NN-` (e.g. `42-fix-foo`)
#
# Prerequisites:
#   vars: MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED (fuse — job skips itself until `true`)
#   branch protection on main with required checks + strict (the machine
#   only merges CLEAN PRs, so protection defines what "ready" means).
#   No secrets needed: github.token is sufficient (merge + issues + PR write).
#   Branch freshness is the SM's job (silent-update-behind); CI on the refreshed
#   head is re-dispatched by the SM (dispatch-only CI — pushes fire no
#   workflows; auto-update-prs.yml is retired).

name: Merge Trigger

run-name: 'Merge Trigger : CI passed → merge pr_approved issues'

on:
  workflow_run:
    workflows: ['CI']
    types: [completed]

permissions:
  contents: write
  pull-requests: write
  issues: write
  actions: read

jobs:
  merge-trigger:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    # Same-repo guard: PRs from forks must not trigger merges.
    if: >-
      github.event.workflow_run.conclusion == 'success' &&
      github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name == github.repository
    concurrency:
      group: merge-trigger-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}-${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_sha }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    steps:
      - name: Gate on MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED
        id: gate
        env:
          ENABLED: ${{ vars.MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED }}
        run: |
          if [ "$ENABLED" = "true" ]; then
            echo "enabled=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "enabled=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "::notice::merge-trigger scaffold is wired but disabled — set the MERGE_TRIGGER_ENABLED repo variable to true (after branch protection + required checks are in place)."
          fi

      - name: Merge issues labeled pr_approved
        if: steps.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.PAT_TOKEN || github.token }}
          LABEL: pr_approved
          CI_RUN_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          repo="${{ github.repository }}"
          issues=$(gh issue list --repo "$repo" --label "$LABEL" --state open \
            --json number --jq '.[].number')
          if [ -z "$issues" ]; then
            echo "no issues labeled '$LABEL' — nothing to merge"
            exit 0
          fi
          merged=0; skipped=0
          for n in $issues; do
            echo "::group::issue #$n"
            pr=$(gh pr list --repo "$repo" --state open \
              --json number,body,headRefName --jq '
              [.[]
                | select(
                    ((.body // "") | test("(?i)\\b(closes|fixes|resolves)\\s+#'"$n"'\\b"))
                    or (.headRefName | test("^'"$n"'[-_.]"))
                  )
                | .number] | first // empty')
            if [ -z "$pr" ]; then
              echo "issue #$n: no linked open PR (add 'Closes #$n' to the PR body or name the branch '$n-…') — skipping"
              skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "::endgroup::"; continue
            fi
            state=$(gh pr view "$pr" --repo "$repo" \
              --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus \
              --jq '.mergeable + ":" + .mergeStateStatus')
            echo "linked PR #$pr — $state"
            case "$state" in
              MERGEABLE:CLEAN)
                if err=$(gh pr merge "$pr" --repo "$repo" --squash 2>&1); then
                  merged=$((merged+1))
                  gh issue edit "$n" --repo "$repo" --remove-label "$LABEL" || true
                  gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$repo" \
                    --body "🔀 Merged #$pr (CI: ${CI_RUN_URL:-run})" || true
                  echo "✅ merged #$pr for issue #$n"
                else
                  skipped=$((skipped+1))
                  echo "❌ merge of #$pr failed: $err"
                fi
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BEHIND)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ behind main — the SM (silent-update-behind) refreshes it, then re-dispatches CI"
                ;;
              MERGEABLE:BLOCKED|MERGEABLE:UNSTABLE)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⏳ required checks not green yet"
                ;;
              *)
                skipped=$((skipped+1)); echo "⛔ not mergeable ($state) — needs manual attention"
                ;;
            esac
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done
          echo "summary: merged=$merged skipped=$skipped"

blocks.text:
# Runner split (2026-09-22): PURE-DART jobs -> ubuntu-24.04-arm (public repo:
# free, SEPARATE capacity pool from the x64 queue). Flutter jobs stay x64 —
# Flutter ships NO official linux-arm64 SDK (stable 3.47.5 manifest is x64
# only; subosito/flutter-action fails 'version: any architecture: arm64').
# cube-kernel-live -> self-hosted M5 (fa-m5-1, user LaunchAgent).
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    tags: ['v*']
  # Dispatch-only CI on PR heads (2026-09 machine-loop redesign): pushes
  # fire NO CI — the SM (machine-sm.yml → factory-sm) is the only trigger.
  # It dispatches this workflow on the PR head when validation is due
  # (validate-fresh / validate-armed rules), so intermediate dev/rework
  # pushes and silent branch updates are free. Required checks still
  # match: the dispatched run registers its check runs on the head SHA.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the binaries job tolerates the
  # double-fire (duplicate create + --clobber upload, last wins).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Main/tag runs are
# never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Issue #177 — a pull request pays only for what it touched:
#   changes  → path classification (union semantics, shared files = full gate)
#   static   → size guard + analyze + publish dry-run        (always, ~1-2 min)
#   test-core→ dart test sharded ×4 (file-level units), per-shard coverage
#              + junit durations (core/shared)
#   coverage-gate → merge shard coverage; PR: diff-coverage, main: full ratchet
#   guards   → CRAP + jscpd + cross-module dupx              (core/shared/app)
#   flutter-analyze → flutter_app analyze on ubuntu          (app/core/shared)
#   flutter-tests → flutter_app tests sharded ×2 on ubuntu   (app/core/shared;
#                   golden suite stays in build-macos.yml — goldens are
#                   host-locked, see issue #177 E5 discussion)
#   test-faui → packages/fa_ui tests sharded ×3 by manifest   (app/core/shared;
#               issue #283 — same template as test-core: manifest assert,
#               per-shard coverage merged to ONE report, junit durations
#               feed shard-rebalance.yml; goldens excluded as before)
#   faui-coverage → merge the 3 fa_ui shard reports into ONE lcov
#                   (issue #283 E3: the gate never sees 3 competing uploads)
#   quality-gate → ONE aggregate required check (skip-tolerant)
#   step-timings → per-step duration telemetry (jobs API → summary+artifact)
#   watchdog   → >2x-baseline timeouts; a timed-out leg means a degraded
#                runner allocation → ONE empty-commit retrigger, never
#                `gh run rerun` (a rerun reallocates into the same pool)
# Tag-only / main-only jobs (publish, binaries, installer-smoke, release,
#   integration) are unchanged in semantics — they just need the new aggregate.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# SEC-08 (#796): explicit minimal default — every job that needs more
# declares its own job-level permissions block.
permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      core: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.core || steps.filter.outputs.core }}
      app: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.app || steps.filter.outputs.app }}
      docs: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.docs || steps.filter.outputs.docs }}
      shared: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.shared || steps.filter.outputs.shared }}
      # PR-only (issue #303): a trajectory-touching diff flips this on so
      # the perf-gate leg below runs the #262 DoD gate per-merge.
      perf: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.perf }}
      # PR-only (issue #551): test/integration/** changes run the no-key
      # mock-LLM integration legs per-PR instead of at tag time only.
      intmock: ${{ steps.paths.outputs.intmock }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # base...head diff for the classifier below
      # Non-PR events (main push, tags, schedule, dispatch): everything is
      # affected — the full gate always guards main and releases.
      - id: filter
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'
        run: |
          echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      # PR classification runs through THE SAME classifier the pre-commit
      # hook uses (issue #194, AC7 + AC5/E2): one source of truth for path
      # rules, and the unknown-path safe default (full gate) — e.g. a new
      # dart_test.yaml at the repo root — now holds in CI, not only in the
      # hook. The selected stage set maps back to the same four groups the
      # old dorny filter emitted.
      - id: paths
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          BASE_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: |
          stages=$(scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run |
            sed -n 's/^Fast gate scope: .*stages://p')
          echo "gate stages:[$stages]"
          # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
          [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ] && stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          case " $stages " in *"flutter"*) echo "app=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"test-core"*) echo "core=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          case " $stages " in *"analyze"*) echo "docs=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # Issue #551: test/integration changes select the mock-LLM leg.
          case " $stages " in *"integration-mock"*) echo "intmock=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" ;; esac
          # All nine stages selected = a shared/unknown path changed:
          if [ -z "$(echo $stages)" ]; then
            # Empty output can only mean detection failure: full gate.
            stages="size analyze test-core coverage crap dup dupx flutter integration-mock"
          fi
          if [ "$(echo $stages | wc -w)" -eq 9 ]; then
            echo "shared=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi
          # Issue #303: the #262 DoD perf gate must red-block the MERGE for
          # trajectory regressions, not only the release — before #551 the
          # only integration leg outside PRs was tag-time. The perf-gate
          # leg re-selects the same gate via --tags perf. Paths = everything
          # the #262 fix touched: ledger core, fa_ui trajectory widgets, CLI
          # trajectory parts, the fah entrypoint, its tests, and the app's
          # session load path.
          if git diff --name-only "$BASE_REF" "$HEAD_REF" |
              grep -qE '(^lib/src/trajectory/|^packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/|^lib/src/cli/trajectory_|^bin/fah\.dart$|^test/(integration/)?trajectory/|^flutter_app/lib/services/agent_service(_sessions)?\.dart$)'; then
            echo "perf=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Issue #709: live kernel-mode cube legs. The ubuntu test-core shards can
  # only prove the SBPL PROFILE TEXT (unit + guard/profile parity) — the
  # kernel's last-match-wins read/write enforcement of rw mounts under a
  # read-denied prefix needs a real `sandbox-exec` run, which exists only on
  # macOS. Both live suites skip with a NAMED reason wherever they…

# Agents — Developer Documentation This directory contains the configuration and JavaScript logic for the **AI-powered Scrum Master (SM) agent system**. The SM agent orchestrates a fully automated software delivery pipeline: it continuously monitors Jira, triggers specialized AI agents for each workflow stage, and manages the complete lifecycle of Stories, Bugs, and Test Cases from Backlog to Done. --- ## Table of Contents 1. [Overview](#overview) 2. [Architecture](#architecture) 3. [Pipeline Diagrams](#pipeline-diagrams) - [Story Pipeline](#story-pipeline) - [Bug Pipeline](#bug-pipeline) - [Test Case Pipeline](#test-case-pipeline) 4. [Full System Overview](#full-system-overview) 5. [SM Rules](#sm-rules) 6. [Agent Configs](#agent-configs) 7. [Key JS Scripts](#key-js-scripts) 8. [Label Lifecycle](#label-lifecycle) 9. [Execution Flow](#execution-flow) --- ## Overview The SM agent system automates the Agile delivery workflow by: - Running on a **20-minute schedule** via GitHub Actions (`sm.yml`) - Scanning Jira using per-rule JQL queries defined in `sm.json` - Dispatching the appropriate agent config (via `ai-teammate.yml` workflow dispatch) or running logic locally for fast/safe operations - Using **label-based locking** to prevent duplicate processing of the same ticket - Supporting three agent types: **Teammate** (CLI agent + prompt), **TestCasesGenerator** (DMTools job), and **JSRunner** (pure JS, no AI) The system covers the full lifecycle: backlog refinement, acceptance criteria generation, solution design, development, PR review, test case generation, test automation, and bug management. --- ## Architecture ### SM Agent Loop The SM agent (`smAgent.js`) is the central orchestrator. Every 20 minutes: 1. Reads all rules from `sm.json` 2. For each enabled rule, runs the JQL query against Jira 3. For each matching ticket, checks `skipIfLabel` — skips the ticket if the label is already present (lock is held) 4. Adds `addLabel` to the ticket (acquires lock) 5. Either dispatches a GitHub Actions `workflow_dispatch` to `ai-teammate.yml` (with `config_file` and `concurrency_key` inputs), executes the JS logic locally (`localExecution: true`), **or** runs the full teammate pipeline synchronously on the local machine (`localTeammate: true`) ### Execution Modes | Mode | When Used | Behavior | |------|-----------|----------| | **Dispatch** (default) | Complex AI tasks (development, review, test gen) | Triggers `ai-teammate.yml` workflow on GitHub Actions; runs asynchronously | | **localExecution: true** | Fast/safe operations (merge checks, status checks) | Runs the postJS directly inside the SM process; synchronous; no AI CLI, no checkout | | **localTeammate: true** | Running the SM/AI Teammate pipeline on a local machine instead of GitHub Actions (e.g. no self-hosted runner available, or for fast local iteration) | Runs `scripts/run-teammate-local.sh`, which calls the same `dmtools run ` entrypoint `ai-teammate.yml` uses — full checkout/branch-switch, AI CLI, PR/Jira actions — but in the calling process. Because it blocks until the script exits, tickets are always processed **one at a time**, regardless of `maxTriggeredWorkflows` (see [Local Execution Flow](#local-teammate-execution-flow-localteammate-true)) | ### Agent Types | Type | Description | |------|-------------| | **Teammate** | Runs a CLI agent (Cursor / GitHub Copilot / Codemie) with a markdown prompt file. `skipAI: true` means AI is driven by the CLI tool, not DMTools AI directly. | | **TestCasesGenerator** | A specialized DMTools job that reads a Jira story/bug and generates structured Test Case tickets (issue type: Test Case) in Jira. | | **JSRunner** | Executes a pure JavaScript file (`jsPath`) with no AI involvement. Used for orchestration (`smAgent.js`) and reporting (`workflowFailureReporter.js`). | ### Concurrency and Locking - **`skipIfLabel`** — SM checks for this label before processing. If present, the ticket is skipped (another run already claimed it). - **`addLabel`** — SM adds this label immediately before dispatching, serving as a distributed lock. - The agent's **postJS** calls `releaseLock()` to remove the label once processing is complete. - The `wip` label (or `_wip`) can be manually applied to any ticket to **pause** SM processing for that ticket indefinitely. --- ## Pipeline Diagrams ### Story Pipeline ```mermaid flowchart TD classDef humanInput fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#92400e,font-weight:bold classDef action fill:#f0f9ff,stroke:#0ea5e9,color:#0c4a6e classDef status fill:#f0fdf4,stroke:#16a34a,color:#14532d s_bl([Backlog]):::status act_q["story_questions.json · dispatch
